pr_title: Sink cache: fix generate from cache
pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #31381. The reason why the script was throwing an error is because input ids were not being cropped to the cache max length, causing size mismatch between inputs and attn mask.

The solution is to crop inputs to the max cache length, which will recompute kv for the whole cache and replace with new kv. Because we cannot infer anymore what was the actual length of the inputs in kv and what should be the length of unprocessed inputs. Yes, we could use '_seen_tokens' but that feature is already deprecated.

Also we need to crop `cache_position` the other way because otherwise the causal mask will not be inferred correctly. 


Tested with the below script. I will add a parameterized to `test_continue from cache` to test that all Cache classes can continue from past_kv and distribute this change to all models, if you think the proposed fix makes sense. IMO it's not the best, but is an option to overcome `cache_position` clash with SinkCache. 

Modifying `cache_position` in generate before forward is not an option, as it will cause cropping inputs using incorrect `cache_position`.

```python
import torch

from transformers import AutoTokenizer,AutoModelForCausalLM
from transformers.cache_utils import SinkCache, DynamicCache

model_id = "meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf"

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
      model_id,
      low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
      device_map='auto',
      attn_implementation="eager", # eager to actually use causal mask and test it works
      torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
)

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, padding_side = 'left')
tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
device = model.device

prefix_list = ["Hello, my name is Raushan and I am", "What's you name?"]
dialog_history = ""
cache = SinkCache(window_length=7, num_sink_tokens=4)

for prefix in prefix_list:
    dialog_history += prefix
    inputs = tokenizer(dialog_history, return_tensors='pt').to(device)
    input_length = inputs.input_ids.shape[-1]

    gen_out = model.generate(**inputs, do_sample=False, max_new_tokens=64,
                            use_cache=True,
                            past_key_values=cache,
                            pad_token_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                            return_dict_in_generate=True,
                            # output_attentions=True,
                        )

    decoded = tokenizer.decode(gen_out.sequences[0, input_length:], skip_special_tokens=True)
    dialog_history += decoded
    cache = gen_out.past_key_values

    print(f"Output: {decoded}")

```

@NiftyliuS hey!

When we use a cache object in the input, the Attention module concatenates the current key-values and the past key-values (from cache) to compute attention scores. That means our attn matrix will be of shape `(new_ids_length, past_kv_length + new_ids_length)`. Therefore if we're using a cache object to iteratively call forward (instead of calling `generate()`) we have to make sure the shape of attention mask is `(batch_size, past_kv_length + new_ids_length)`

In you case, you either
- have to crop your inputs to " General Kenobi!" because you already have "Hello there!" key-values saved in cache. And prepare attn mask for "Hello there! General Kenobi!"
- Simply extend attn mask to the length of "Hello there!Hello there! General Kenobi!"

Hope this clarifies your question! Btw, it's not the first time people are confused about using a cache object outside `generate()`, so I am considering making a better doc on that :)

Yes, generate() has more going under the hood to prepare inputs for the next forward, for example in these lines
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/6fbea6d237cbdfc3c229cdadfa3c968cfb2d5142/src/transformers/models/llama/modeling_llama.py#L1116-L1125

For the attention mask, we don't crop it usually and use the whole attention mask, while the input ids and position ids are cropped takking into account the length of past seen key/values. 

But you're using SinkCache, so as @gante mentioned, we still have to ensure that the mask doesn't go beyond the cache max length. That means we will discard old mask tokens as soon as the length exceeds `max_cache_length`. Same will go for StaticCache object :)

Okay, according to the comment I added above, we won't accept inputs larger than the context window. This means that, when the cache is full and we are in a multi-round generation, `input_ids` fed to `generate` must be exclusively the new user prompt (otherwise, by logical necessity, the length of `input_ids` is larger than the cache's context window).

Therefore, in addition to the code you added here, let's:
1. In the exception added in the `SinkCache`, let's add this case (e.g. "If you are doing multi-round generation, ensure that `input_ids` passed to `generate` is exclusively the new user input")
2. Add a comment next to the exception to check this PR for more information
3. Simplify the comment here for our future selves :D e.g.
```
            # In `SinkCache` we can't rely on `cache.get_seq_length()` to get the sequence length when it is full. In that case, assume we are doing multi-round generation AND the input only contains new tokens. See the exception raised in `SinkCache` for more information.
```

Together, the exception and this comment will set well-defined boundaries of what `SinkCache` accepts (this comment), explain to the user what to do if they don't respect the assumption (exception),  and provide a reference in case someone wants to dive (comment to the exception)
